summary: Who decides, how to decide, what to do first, and how architecture serves the product.

items.text: Ask what it costs to reverse a decision. Go fast on two-way doors and slowly on one-way doors.
Name one decider before the discussion starts. Input is not approval.
Use a single owner with advice, such as DACI, for most decisions. Keep consensus for few decisions.
Agree the criteria before you score the options, and set a deadline.
Give each shared product and architecture decision one decider anyway.
Disagree once, before the decision. Then commit, and reopen only with new facts.
Write a revisit trigger with each decision. Record a reversal as a new entry.
Give each row exactly one A.
Give each row at least one R. A and R can be the same person.
Keep C small. Each C adds a conversation and a delay.
Send I a message. Do not invite I to the meeting.
Use verbs as rows and roles as columns, not names.
Fill in A first, then R, then C and I.
A column with no empty cells is overloaded. A column with only I is perhaps not needed.

items.when: You have a long, unsorted list and a short workshop
You must fix the scope of one release or time box
items.use: MoSCoW, with Musts at no more than about 60% of effort

items.when: You compare many product ideas and timing matters little
Items differ in urgency, deadlines, or weekly loss
items.use: Cost of delay divided by duration (CD3 or WSJF)

items.when: You balance a release across basic, performance, and delighter features
Technical debt or platform work competes with features
items.use: Cost of delay, a capacity share, or an error budget

items.text: Start from the user problem and the business result, not from the feature.
Steer the team by outcomes. An output can have no effect.
Reduce the four risks before you build: value, usability, feasibility, and viability.
Put problems on the roadmap with order and confidence, not features with dates.
Test the riskiest assumption first. An MVP is not a bad version 1.
Give each main metric at least one guardrail metric.
Tie each characteristic and design choice to a product goal. State its cost per user or per order.
